- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently underpredicts true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 1–3% upward bias for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model exhibits high variance; use 10-day rolling mean as baseline for correction.
- Forecast errors cluster around 70–75 range; if true price exceeds 72, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust for 3–5 day lag in upward momentum.
